title: Navigating Siblings
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of navigating siblings in a jQuery application.
Apply .siblings() in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify .next() and .nextall() with an explicit test or browser observation.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through navigating siblings with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns .siblings() into a repeatable implementation choice. Traversal starts from an existing selection and moves through its ancestors, descendants, or siblings. Scope traversal to the component you mean instead of repeating broad document-wide queries.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
